what_happened.line: Town Meeting spent its longest debate on an amendment to cover a school budget gap, first from roads and then from the reserve fund; the result is not audible.
Articles 1 to 6 on the consent calendar passed, and articles 10 and 11 on collective bargaining were proposed to be passed over because no agreements were reached.
The FY15 budget as printed went to a vote, but the outcome is not audible in the captions.
The Lane property purchase for conservation, which needs a two-thirds vote and depends on a state grant, was taken up; the vote is not audible.
The sewer service area map, article 17 and article 29 passed unanimously; votes on right to farm and the liquor license provision are not audible.

why_it_matters: The FY15 budget sets the town's spending, mostly paid by taxes, and the school gap debate shows a choice between school funding, road repair and the reserve fund that covers emergencies.
Several results, including the budget, the Lane purchase and the right to farm bylaw, cannot be confirmed from the captions, so the official town record is the place to check them.

meetings.headline: Town Meeting heard the new 6-12 school project and a marijuana moratorium; vote results are not in the captions.
meetings.summary: The special town meeting took up Article 1, a borrowing appropriation for a new combined grades 6-12 middle/high school with state building authority funding. A debt exclusion ballot vote was set for Saturday. Presentations covered building condition, options, site plan, schedule and tax impact, and public comment was mostly supportive. Article 2, a medical marijuana zoning definition and one-year moratorium, drew long debate. The captions end as the moderator begins the vote, so no outcomes are audible.

what_happened.line: Article 1, a borrowing appropriation for a new combined grades 6-12 school, was presented; the captions do not carry the vote result.
A debt exclusion ballot vote on the school borrowing was set for the Saturday after this town meeting.
Presentations compared a do-nothing repair path, renovation options and a new 6-12 school, with state building authority funding and a tax impact estimate.
Article 2, a medical marijuana zoning definition and one-year moratorium, drew long debate, with speakers on both sides and a suggestion to return in May.
The moderator moved to vote on Article 2, which needs two-thirds; the captions end before the outcome.

why_it_matters: If the school borrowing is approved at the ballot, the debt is paid through a debt exclusion, which raises property tax bills for the life of the loan, with the state grant reducing the amount borrowed.
Article 2 decides whether medical marijuana businesses can be sited under the existing zoning or must wait a year while the town writes rules.
watch_next: The debt exclusion ballot vote on the school project, set for Saturday the 11th.
The recorded outcomes of Articles 1 and 2, which the captions do not show; the official town meeting results would confirm them.
